decision: scoped this as the doc's phase A plus phase B only: fix the false completion marking and add structural chunking; phases C-F (parsers, citations, topic routing, conflicts) are explicitly out
why: phase A alone would only stop the lie about completion, not the truncation; A+B is the smallest slice where long-document coverage is actually true

decision: definition of done: a 30k-character file has its tail fact reach the model, a file set over the request budget completes in batches with unprocessed parts still visible, and a mid-run failure never marks a source complete and its retry neither skips nor repeats a chunk
why: three falsifiable claims, each checked against the real CLI as a subprocess, not against a helper

decision: ran the existing suite before touching anything and recorded it green at 64 tests
why: every later check needs to read as old value against new value

decision: wrote the gate tests first and confirmed they fail
why: the failing test is the specification; it also proves the suite cannot pass by accident

decision: put the chunker in a new skills/lw/scripts/chunking.py rather than growing wiki.py
why: wiki.py is already a 583-line script that already duplicates a copy in the plugin; a separate pure module keeps the offsets logic testable without a wiki directory

decision: represented a chunk as offsets plus text plus a verbatim flag, with heading_path as a tuple stored beside the text and never inside it
why: the doc warns that inserting heading paths into the body shifts offsets; the flag is what makes a repeated table header or fence honest instead of a silent offset lie

decision: made the planner the single source of truth for what to ingest: one entry per source carrying chunks plus chunks_total and chunks_done, and the state.json file records are derived from it
why: the bug is that apply_update hashed all records regardless of what was submitted, so two places decided what was done; the planner is the one decision point

decision: modelled the resumable work as an on-disk run manifest under .llm-wiki/runs/ with a per-chunk done flag, deleted only when the whole run commits
why: the doc requires a replayable pending list; a manifest makes the retry path a reload rather than a reimplementation, and the doc's wiki_ingest_runs/wiki_ingest_results tables are the online equivalent

decision: did not adopt the doc's new wiki_source_revisions / wiki_parses / wiki_chunks SQLite tables
why: this is the local CLI whose stores are state.json and Markdown, and phases A-B do not touch SharedWikiStore at all; the doc lists those tables for the online D-F phases

decision: kept v1 state.json readable and upgraded it in place, marking every previously-recorded file unverified with a reason
why: the old hashes were written for files that may have been truncated or skipped, so trusting them preserves exactly the bug being fixed; re-ingesting once is the safe direction because a duplicate is cheaper than a lost fact

decision: found that skills/lw and plugins/llm-wiki/skills/lw are two hand-edited copies and nothing checked they match; the running MCP executes the plugin one
why: a fix applied to one copy would ship silently to nobody or to half the callers
result: parity test added, single-writer rule set

decision: gave the chunker to a subagent with a frozen interface and a file scope limited to the one new module, keeping the gate tests, the mirror, the wiki.py integration and every commit myself
why: review separation for the mechanical pass, one writer for the shared files so the two copies cannot race

decision: chunker committed as 51c61a3 after amending: the first attempt captured the two copies one line apart
why: my commit raced the delegate's refactor and captured a dead field in only one copy; a copy pair that differs at HEAD defeats the whole point of the parity test

decision: deleted the unused _Block.fence field and its dead assignment in both copies rather than keeping the delegate's version
why: the field is assigned but never read; removing it is the smaller honest artifact and it removes the reason the two copies had diverged

decision: mutation-checked the chunking gate: removing the final flush, the hard cap, or the table header each turns it red
why: a gate that cannot fail is not a gate; I need to know it observes the behaviour it claims
result: M1 34 failures, M2 37, M3 6; restored green

decision: added a seeded 60-case fuzz test over random heading/fence/table/paragraph documents
why: hand-written fixtures cannot cover the boundary shapes where an offset bug hides, and the fuzz immediately caught an imprecise helper of mine

decision: wiki.py rewritten around a chunk-batch-commit pipeline; the old apply_update and source_bundle are deleted
why: the bug lived in apply_update hashing all records regardless of what was submitted; leaving it beside the new path would leave two answers to what is done

decision: found by reading the delegate diff that a retry reused the done-flags but threw away the pages earlier batches had produced
why: the delegate's own tests passed because chunk reuse is what it checked; nobody checked that the surviving chunks' knowledge reached the page

decision: rejected the delegate's top-level evidence field in the HTTP body and taught the test stub to read the prompt instead
why: it duplicated the whole material payload on every request to make a test scrape easier, which is real API cost for no product reason

decision: reverted the delegate's addition of .log to the eligible extensions and moved my fixture to .md
why: widening what the wiki ingests is a product change the request did not ask for; the test should follow the product, not bend it
result: extension list back to the original set

decision: kept plan_ingest, create_run and commit_run free of unused parameters, and dropped the per-unit drift check that became redundant once pruning existed
why: an unused parameter is a claim in the signature that the body does not honour
evidence: commit d01a2fc; `git show d01a2fc:skills/lw/scripts/wiki.py` shows no root/state parameter on any of the three
result: no unused params remain (AST pass clean)

decision: ran the comment review and accepted two of its three actionable findings, rejected the rest with reasons
why: it wanted test docstrings and the material_budget unit contract deleted; those state each test's purpose and a public unit, but its manifest-key and magic-number findings were right
result: 2 accepted fixes landed, remainder rejected on the merits

decision: ran the full suite from a clean worktree at HEAD with no untracked files present
why: the local tree could be passing because of files that were never committed
result: 115 tests pass from tracked state alone

decision: cross-model review of this trail and diff; it found by running the code that a deleted source wedges every later retry and that two manifests resolve arbitrarily
why: the reviewer's scripts reproduced both, which no committed test had done

decision: abandoned-source pruning: units of a source whose bytes moved are dropped so the run converges and the source is planned again next run
why: an unusable run must not become a permanent wedge; convergence with a retry is the property the manifest exists for

decision: load_run picks the newest manifest instead of sorted()[0], and the v1 upgrade writes state.v1.json and raises WikiError on a malformed record
why: a crash that leaves two manifests must not silently replay the older one, and a rewrite in place needs a copy to compare against

decision: update now prints the same skipped-file lines status does
why: the doc requires a skipped file to appear with its reason, and update is the command users run
evidence: commit 89b7eb2, verified against the real CLI

decision: checked all three Phase A claims against the real CLI as a subprocess, and added the two e2e coverage gaps the review named
why: the definition of done named these three, so they get checked on the shipped artifact rather than a helper; the 30k boundary and partial-visibility claims were under-asserted
